A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same self-evolving-agent survey, with matching core taxonomy and equations. Text, tables, figures, and references support reliable comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 surveys existing systems and benchmarks. Its performance statements are attributed to prior work; it reports no original empirical study.

after.justification: v4 remains a survey. Its new numerical examples and comparative tables synthesize cited studies, while the evaluation protocols are recommendations rather than original experimental results.

M1.justification: Neither version proposes an implemented agent algorithm or model. Expanded descriptions of existing methods and new operational inclusion criteria do not change a proposed computational procedure.

E1.justification: Neither version actually conducts training or evaluation on datasets. DS-Bench, EvaLearn, AutoEnv, and other additions expand surveyed literature, rather than the work's experimental dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates baselines against a proposed method. v4 Table 11 newly collates published comparisons, but does not introduce an experimental baseline evaluation by this work.

E3.justification: Beyond v1's broad assessment categories, v4 Section 7.2.4 and Table 10 specify proposed protocols covering state resets versus persistence, per-task and cumulative budgets, retention probes, OOD evaluation, and cost and safety measures. These are substantive evaluation-design recommendations, not evidence of rerun experiments.

E4.justification: v4 Table 10 adds a focused literature-based case study checking EvoAgent against the proposed long-horizon protocol, identifying supported features and missing retention, cost, and safety reporting. Neither version reports original ablation or robustness experiments.

E5.justification: Neither version reports run counts, actual seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for an original evaluation. v4 recommends seed logging and criticizes limited repetitions in cited benchmarks, without adding uncertainty estimates to its reported comparisons.

E6.justification: v4 adds substantial quantitative literature synthesis through Tables 5, 10, and 11 and Section 7.1.6. For example, Table 11 newly lists GSM8K scores of 90.5%, 90.8%, and 94.6% for ADAS, AFlow, and ScoreFlow with GPT-4o-mini. These are newly tabulated cited results under partially matched settings, not v1-to-v4 performance gains.

T1.justification: v4 Section 7.1.2 corrects the transposed task/time indices in the forgetting and backward-transfer formulas to match the stated definition of J_i,t. The POMDP formulation and evolution/objective equations (1)-(3) remain unchanged; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The central survey contribution and what/when/how framework remain. v4 qualifies the work as a guiding synthesis of an emerging field, emphasizes autonomy as the defining distinction, and softens categorical ASI-precursor language in the introduction and conclusion.

C2.justification: v4 substantially expands interpretations and limitations: operational boundaries and autonomy levels, distinctions between self-play and imitation, benchmark coverage gaps, obstacles to fair comparisons, personalization/privacy trade-offs, and evolution-specific model, memory, and tool risks. Sections 7.3 and 8.3 provide much more concrete qualifications and mitigation guidance than v1.

D1.justification: New worked examples disclose source-attributed configurations and resource information, including backbone models in Table 11 and EvoAgent's reported A100 hardware and training times in Table 10. The survey repository link remains unchanged, and no new implementation or data release is documented.

R1.justification: v4 adds substantial historical positioning through genetic algorithms, genetic programming, Sims, and NEAT, alongside newer memory, self-play, and safety literature. Section 2.2 also replaces v1's overly categorical lifelong-learning distinction with a discussion acknowledging replay and episodic memory.

P1.justification: Evaluation is reorganized into goal-specific metrics and coverage-gap subsections, while safety is rewritten around emergent risks and mitigation strategies. Positioning and methodological explanations are extensively expanded, the contents pages are removed, and the title and citation style change.

P2.justification: v4 adds five tables covering costs, coverage gaps, protocols, comparative performance, and deployment safeguards; revises Figures 1, 3, and 4; and expands several captions. Existing metric and horizon-comparison tables are retained and renumbered within the new journal layout.

improvement.justification: Operational inclusion criteria, the corrected lifelong-learning comparison, historical grounding, and substantially stronger evaluation and safety analysis address important conceptual and practical weaknesses in v1. These gains outweigh localized problems in the new quantitative material: notably, Table 10 incorrectly calls 21.80% to 30.29% a 105.9% relative gain, although those values imply about 38.9%.
